title: POST /context-snapshot crashes on real Claude Code payloads (current_usage is an object, not a number)
description:
The /context-snapshot handler in cch.server expects context_window.current_usage to be a number (legacy statusLine schema), but Claude Code now sends it as an object: {input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens}.

Result: log/log-context-snapshot! does (long current-tokens) → ClassCastException → 500 to caller, no row inserted. This is the 'sparse snapshots' issue tracked under claude-code-hooks-57e — diagnostic log shows 732/734 invocations returning HTTP 500.
design: Treat current_usage robustly: if it's a number use it directly; if it's a map sum its numeric values; otherwise nil. The indexed column is a convenience — full payload is already in the JSON blob, so being lenient at the boundary is correct. Add a unit test covering each schema shape.
close_reason: Closed

title: Run cch from self-contained runtime, install to ~/.local/bin, drop repo symlink
description: Decouple the cch control plane from the dev checkout. Root cause of the 2026-08-31 outage was ~/.local/share/cch/repo symlink dangling after repo rename, and ~/bin/cch running 'clj -M:cli' from that repo. Decision: everything (services + codex MCP + cch CLI) runs the self-contained jlink runtime at ~/.local/share/cch/runtime/bin/cch; shim installed to ~/.local/bin; no repo symlink. Ship code changes via 'just build && just install'; dev-hack via 'clj -M:cli' in the repo directly. Touch: scripts/install (shim delegates to runtime, drop symlink, default ~/.local/bin), control_runner_service.clj + cch.service renderer (ExecStart/WorkingDirectory -> runtime/stable paths), codex_settings.clj (MCP command -> runtime path). Then rebuild, redeploy, migrate on-disk units + codex config, restart services, remove ~/bin/cch + repo symlink.
close_reason: Done: cch runs from self-contained jlink runtime via ~/.local/bin/cch shim; services + codex MCP + hooks all re-pointed; ~/bin/cch and repo symlink removed. Also fixed a jlink regression (added jdk.httpserver module for plumcp). Verified: MCP handshake, doctor ok, 470 tests pass.

title: Codex adapter misses live threads on app-server 0.151 (thread/loaded/list)
description: cch's codex adapter (src/cch/control/codex.clj sessions-with-client) enumerates live sessions via thread/list {:useStateDbOnly true} then removes notLoaded. On codex app-server 0.151 the state-DB rows are all notLoaded (persisted rollouts), so this returns []. 0.151 added a dedicated thread/loaded/list method that returns live thread ids; details come from thread/read. Fix: enumerate loaded ids via thread/loaded/list (paginated via nextCursor), thread/read each, map through public-thread. Verified 2026-08-31: a live idle vscode codex thread was invisible to cch/sessions while thread/loaded/list returned it.
close_reason: Fixed: codex adapter now enumerates live threads via thread/loaded/list + thread/read (0.151). Verified live: cx/sessions surfaces the loaded codex thread; doctor codex protocol ok.

The hosted surface should be the familiar cch web application promoted to fleet scope: a shared visual shell, global agent control, privacy-safe global events, and the full usage experience over normalized broker data. Hooks, hook configuration, raw payloads, and debug facilities remain runner-local.

Runner diagnostics may be reachable through one contextual runner link, not a hosted Local tools directory.

title: Bound Codex Stop usage capture memory on large rollouts
description: The Codex Stop hook currently slurps and parses the entire rollout JSONL into a vector to find the latest token_count event. Large, long-running sessions expand beyond the dispatcher's bounded JVM heap, causing OutOfMemoryError on /dispatch/Stop. The agent then reports invalid Stop hook JSON because the HTTP request fails before a protocol response is produced.
design: Prefer a reverse or bounded tail scan that stops after finding the newest valid event_msg/token_count record. Do not load the complete transcript or retain parsed unrelated events.
acceptance_criteria: Codex usage capture finds the latest relevant token_count event with bounded memory independent of rollout size; large synthetic rollouts do not exhaust a 256 MB heap; Stop returns valid hook JSON or a neutral response; regression tests cover large and malformed trailing JSONL records.
notes: Implemented a reverse chunked JSONL scanner with a fixed read buffer and a one-record cap. Malformed, unterminated, and oversized trailing records are skipped; the newest valid token_count record is returned without parsing unrelated transcript history. Full suite passes (404 tests, 1166 assertions). Real rollouts larger than 60 MB and 380 MB were scanned successfully under a 64 MB heap in single-digit milliseconds. The rebuilt managed server returned HTTP 200 with neutral JSON for a real large-rollout Stop request in about 13 ms with no new server error.
close_reason: Bounded reverse scan implemented, regression-tested, exercised against large real rollouts, and deployed to both active hook dispatchers.

title: Verify live agent-originated MCP routing across runners
description: Run the final POC acceptance test with a registered native agent invoking the restricted cch MCP send_message tool itself across the hosted broker. Verify authenticated agent source ownership, delivery into a live agent on another runner, and an agent-originated reply or observable receipt. Operator-originated CLI sends do not satisfy this test.
acceptance_criteria: A registered Codex or Claude invokes cch send_message through MCP without shell/CLI fallback; the broker records the leased agent route as source and delivers once to a live route on another runner; receipt or reply is observed and no message body is persisted.
notes: Live acceptance passed across two remote runners. A registered Codex invoked cch send_message through MCP without shell fallback; the broker recorded its leased Codex route and delivered on the first attempt to a live Claude route. A fresh registered Claude then used only ToolSearch and cch send_message; the broker recorded its leased Claude route and delivered on the first attempt to the live Codex, which visibly acknowledged the matching marker. Agent logs contained no Bash tool call. The Postgres messages table contains only message/route identifiers, content digest, delivery state, attempts, failure, and timestamps; it has no body column. Compatibility coverage passes in the full suite (400 tests, 1158 assertions).
close_reason: Live bidirectional agent-originated MCP routing and receipt verified; metadata-only persistence confirmed.

title: Do not restart active Codex app-server during control install
description: The one-time control installer always runs systemctl restart after reconciling MCP and hook configuration. Re-running it while ordinary Codex clients are attached disconnects every client from the shared app-server even when the generated unit is unchanged. Configuration reconciliation must be non-disruptive by default.
design: Install or update the unit atomically, daemon-reload, enable it, and start it only when inactive. If the unit changed while the service is already active, leave the running process untouched and report that a deliberate later restart is required. A separate explicit restart path may be added when production UX needs it.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running control install against an active unchanged service performs no restart; an inactive service is enabled and started; an active service with a changed unit is not restarted implicitly and returns an actionable status; tests cover every branch without touching a real service.
notes: Implemented non-disruptive service reconciliation. Install now checks active/enabled state, atomically updates changed units, reloads systemd metadata only when needed, enables only when disabled, and starts only when inactive. An active changed unit returns restart-required without restarting; an active unchanged unit is untouched. Live validation against an active service preserved both PID and start timestamp. Full suite passes (374 tests, 1062 assertions); focused lint is clean; uberjar builds.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bind Codex MCP calls to their native source thread
description: A Codex agent can call the cch MCP server and successfully route text, but the tested CLI does not expose its native thread id to the child MCP process. When source is omitted, cch therefore reports operator rather than the calling Codex route. Find a supported, non-spoofable binding between each Codex MCP invocation and its native app-server thread; do not infer identity from message content or persist provider credentials.
acceptance_criteria: A message initiated through cch by each of two concurrent Codex sessions is attributed to the correct codex route without the model supplying a trusted source claim; a missing or ambiguous binding fails clearly instead of silently becoming operator; tests cover concurrent callers and restart behavior.
notes: Implemented a supported Codex PreToolUse-to-MCP binding. The hook receives the native session id and tool-use id, stores only one-time routing metadata plus a body digest, and overwrites the reserved source_proof field. The MCP server atomically consumes the exact envelope binding and fails clearly for missing, mismatched, expired, or replayed proofs. Live validation used two simultaneous synthetic Codex sessions sending in both directions; each receiver displayed the correct peer route, and Codex still showed its normal MCP approval prompt.
close_reason: Codex caller attribution is bound to native PreToolUse session and tool-use identifiers, is envelope-matched and one-time, and passed two-client live validation.

title: POC: route native sessions across two machines
description: Prove the local routing mechanism through a disposable in-memory broker between two paired runners over Tailscale HTTPS. Do not add Postgres, Google OAuth, transcript storage, or production deployment machinery.
design: Disposable control-plane POC: a standalone in-memory HTTP broker owns only leased opaque route presence and transient message envelopes. Each runner authenticates with a persistent per-runner pairing token, registers sanitized local routes, and polls outbound so agents require no per-start auth and runners need no inbound port. Broker retries unacked messages with bounded attempts/expiry; runners deliver through native local adapters and ack idempotently. Local routing remains authoritative and functional when broker is absent. No provider credentials, transcripts, cwd/path data, or durable broker database.
acceptance_criteria: Codex-to-Codex and Codex-to-Claude messages cross between runner A and runner B; replies return; reconnect, bounded retry, expiry, and duplicate suppression work; the disposable broker can be disabled without affecting native sessions.
notes:
Implemented the disposable broker/runner slice: authenticated per-runner route leases, sanitized presence, transient in-memory envelopes, outbound polling, terminal acks, bounded retry/expiry, source ownership checks, restart-safe duplicate replay, optional MCP/CLI routing, and local-only fallback. Synthetic HTTP integration covers Codex-to-Codex, Codex-to-Claude, and a return reply across two logical runners. Full suite passes (369 tests, 1048 assertions); focused new-code lint is clean; uberjar builds. The all-files lint gate still reports pre-existing warnings outside this changeset. Keep this bead open until the same matrix is exercised over Tailscale HTTPS on two physical machines.
Physical two-host POC passed over tailnet-private HTTPS. Native Codex-to-Codex request and MCP reply each crossed the broker once, were acknowledged in one attempt, persisted in the exact destination threads, and returned idle. The physical Codex-to-Claude and Claude-to-Codex paths also passed. Provider login and the narrowly scoped cch.send_message trust grant are one-time per machine, not per agent start. Codex 0.149 may require a TUI repaint to display turns started by another app-server client, but its native thread wakes, processes, persists, and replies correctly; 0.150 displayed remote input directly. No provider credentials, hostnames, account data, filesystem paths, or transcript content are stored by the broker or added here.
Final gates: 371 tests / 1052 assertions pass, focused control-runner lint is clean, and the uberjar builds. The runner now reports distinct polling failures and suppresses only consecutive repeats, making tailnet/broker faults diagnosable while preserving reconnect behavior.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decide go/no-go on native control-plane architecture
description: Evaluate the local and cross-machine POC evidence before production work begins. Record whether supported native interfaces are reliable enough and materially simpler than a universal terminal relay.
design: Approve only if ordinary startup has no per-session cch chore, delivery uses supported or generated native interfaces, approvals remain provider-native, cross-machine delivery is idempotent, and version drift degrades safely.
acceptance_criteria: Record a go or no-go decision with evidence; explicitly close, supersede, or re-scope every affected legacy federation bead; leave production children blocked on a no-go.
notes: GO decision (2026-08-27): proceed with the native-first multi-agent local execution control plane. Physical Codex-to-Codex and Codex-to-Claude routing crossed two machines through the tailnet-private broker, including an idempotent request/reply cycle. Ordinary agent startup required no per-session cch credential or pairing chore after one-time machine setup. Codex delivery used the generated App Server protocol and Claude delivery used native hooks/inbox integration; provider-native approval boundaries remained intact. Version drift between tested Codex releases changed presentation behavior but preserved delivery and persistence semantics. This is materially simpler and safer than PTY multiplexing because the control plane does not parse ANSI terminal streams or centralize provider credentials/transcripts. Production caveats are explicitly tracked in vgi.4-vgi.8: capability diagnostics, supervision, reconnect/replay bounds, least-privilege Postgres, install/trust UX, and migration parity. Federation is re-scoped, not discarded: normalized control-plane events belong in the broker, while forecast inputs move through a narrow usage-observation stream; existing table federation remains only until parity.
close_reason: GO: physical native-interface POC passed; legacy federation scope has been explicitly superseded or preserved in vgi.8.

title: Native-first multi-agent control plane: Claude + Codex
description: Build a native-first session switchboard and routing control plane for Claude and Codex. Preserve provider terminals, authentication, approvals, transcripts, worktrees, and remote-control surfaces. A local and cross-machine proof of concept is a hard gate before production infrastructure.
design: Use supported Claude inbox and Remote Control facilities, Codex app-server and queue facilities, a local stdio MCP server, paired runners, and a central broker. Do not use PATH shims, PTY interception, terminal emulation, or centralized provider transcripts.
acceptance_criteria: The POC gate passes; production runner, MCP routing, broker, web switchboard, federation migration, and product documentation are completed; tracked artifacts contain synthetic deployment and identity data only.
notes: Milestone: the native-first architecture passed its hard POC gate. Live registered Codex and Claude sessions each originated restricted cch MCP messages across separate runners through the central broker; leased source identity, first-attempt delivery, observable receipt, and metadata-only durable storage were verified. The project can proceed from feasibility testing to production control-plane rollout.

title: POC: local native Claude/Codex discovery and routing
description: Prove on one machine that ordinary Claude and Codex sessions can be discovered and can exchange messages through supported native interfaces and a local cch MCP server. Exclude Postgres, OAuth, public deployment, transcript federation, terminal wrapping, and polished UI.
design: Use a lightweight Claude SessionStart hook to register the native inbox address locally; connect directly to Codex app-server using WebSocket-over-UDS for discovery and thread/queue/add delivery; use a pinned PluMCP stdio server with list_sessions, get_session, and send_message. On Linux, supervise the packaged Codex app-server over its default Unix socket with a cch-installed systemd user unit. Do not use app-server proxy as a JSONL transport, enable Codex Remote Control during the local POC, or depend on OpenAI's standalone installer/updater loop.
acceptance_criteria: Two ordinary Codex sessions and one ordinary Claude session register without cch launch commands; Codex-to-Codex and both Codex-to-Claude directions work; source attribution is visible; duplicates are idempotent; approval or permission responses cannot be relayed; restarts and unsupported versions fail clearly.
notes: Local native-control proof completed with two simultaneous Codex clients and one Claude session. Synthetic messages succeeded for Codex-to-Codex, Codex-to-Claude, and Claude-to-Codex; both Codex callers were attributed to their own native routes through one-time PreToolUse bindings. Duplicate ids, stale Claude delivery, app-server restart and reconnect, environment reconciliation, and the no-permission-relay boundary were validated. No provider credentials or message bodies are persisted. Codex currently joins the shared native server with codex --remote unix://; improving that launch UX is a separate product decision.

title: Forecast bg-refresh pins a core: per-event refresh × unindexed full scans

title: Codex 0% snapshots poison /usage window selection
description: Codex sessions report two rate-limit states per turn: one with the real weekly resets_at and real percentages, another with 0.0% and a rolling resets_at (now + 7d). The 0.0% entries have unique resets_at values (1 sample each), while the real data shares a fixed resets_at (14+ samples). latest-resets-at picks the most recent row's resets_at, which is usually a 0.0% one, so the pipeline filters to only that single 0.0% sample. Fix: skip 0.0% in codex-usage-capture, and make latest-resets-at prefer non-zero samples.

description: The local CCH UI has become slow at the current database size, especially the events page which takes roughly 10–15 seconds. Benchmark all server endpoints against the current SQLite data, identify the dominant nearby bottleneck, implement a targeted fix, and add regression coverage.

title: Usage page: 5h ↔ 7d window toggle (prep for multi-CLI)
description:
## Why

The user is now running both Claude (\$200 plan, 7d window dominant) and Codex (\$20 plan, 5h window dominant). Today the /usage page only renders the 7d window. To make the page useful for Codex once the multi-CLI integration lands (ql4), we need to expose both windows with a toggle.

Doing this before ql4 also de-risks the multi-CLI work: it forces the Bayesian projection / chart code to demonstrably work on the 5h window with real data we already collect.

## Scope

1. Refactor src/cch/forecast.clj: make build-current-window + current-window take a window-key (:five-hour | :seven-day). Cache per window-key. Reuse the existing window-config priors and the already-parameterized compute-window-stats helpers where possible. rate-5h-samples enrichment stays nil for 5h-native view (raw observed samples are already 60s-bucketed).
2. Refactor src/cch/usage.clj rendering: time-axis ticks switch on window (day ticks for 7d, hour ticks for 5h). Stat tile labels reflect the window. Rest of chart code (projection band, observed line, gridlines) stays as-is.
3. src/cli/cch.clj handle-usage: accept ?window=5h|7d query param; default 7d for now (per-agent default deferred to 9a2 once we have :agent column).
4. Page header: simple [5h] [7d] toggle (two anchor tags swapping the query param). No client-side JS.
5. Tests in test/cch/usage_test.clj: build-data returns coherent shapes for both windows; toggle param round-trips through handler.

## Out of scope

- Per-agent default (5h for codex, 7d for claude). Needs :agent column from 9a2.
- Learned prior for 5h window. window-config :five-hour hardcoded priors are good enough for v1; can derive from history later (~33 completed windows/week available).
- Cross-CLI pooling of window data — single agent only for now.

## Acceptance

- /usage and /usage?window=7d render today's page.
- /usage?window=5h renders the same shape with 5h data, hour ticks, projection band, stat tiles.
- Toggle buttons in the header swap views.
- just test passes.

title: Fix fork bomb regex false positive on compound redirects
description: command-guard fork bomb pattern matched '2>/dev/null &&' because && starts with & and the regex lacked a negative lookahead. Benign commands like 'ls /path 2>/dev/null && echo exists' were blocked as fork bombs. Fixed by adding (?!&) lookahead to the pattern. Observed 44+ false positive blocks in 7 days across all repos.
close_reason: Closed

title: Split hook response renderer by event type (not PreToolUse-only)
description:
## Context

`src/cch/protocol.clj` hardcodes the PreToolUse response shape (`hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision`). Every other Claude Code hook event uses a different output schema, so cch can today only drive PreToolUse hooks correctly — a PostToolUse, Stop, PermissionRequest, or WorktreeCreate hook built on the current framework would produce malformed JSON that Claude Code ignores or warns about.

Per the current Claude Code hooks reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), response shapes fall into four groups:

1. **PreToolUse** — `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` (current implementation).
2. **Top-level `decision`/`reason`** — PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SubagentStop, UserPromptSubmit, ConfigChange, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted.
3. **`hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior`** (plus `updatedInput`/`updatedPermissions`) — PermissionRequest.
4. **Stdout path** (command type) or **`hookSpecificOutput.worktreePath`** (http type) — WorktreeCreate.

Plus ~15 side-effect-only events with no decision control (SessionStart/End, Notification, PreCompact/PostCompact, CwdChanged, FileChanged, InstructionsLoaded, etc.) that still need a nil-safe renderer path so a hook subscribed to them doesn't produce garbage output.

## Why this is highest-leverage

Every other roadmap item (HTTP/prompt/agent hook types, universal event observer, any second built-in hook on a non-PreToolUse event) needs this split before it can land correctly. Doing this first unlocks all of them with one change.

## Design

Replace the hardcoded renderer with dispatch keyed on event name. Two shape options:

- **`defmulti` on event name**, with a default no-op method for side-effect events. More idiomatic Clojure; easier to extend with new events one PR at a time.
- **Map from event-name → renderer fn**. Simpler to enumerate at a glance; slightly less ergonomic to grow.

Either works. `defmulti` recommended.

Each renderer takes the pure decision map from the hook function (e.g. `{:decision :deny :reason "..."}` or `nil`) and returns the JSON-serializable map matching that event's output schema.

`defhook` wrapper in `src/cch/core.clj` needs to pass the event name through to the renderer — currently it's effectively hardcoded via the hook's metadata and the single renderer path.

Keep the pure-check-function pattern intact. Hook functions still return `nil` / `{:decision ...}` data; only the renderer changes.

## Files to touch

- `src/cch/protocol.clj` — replace `->response` with event-keyed dispatch.
- `src/cch/core.clj` — `defhook` macro threads event name to renderer.
- `test/cch/protocol_test.clj` — add a deftest per renderer branch.

## Acceptance

- `protocol/->response` dispatches on event name and produces spec-compliant JSON for at least: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, PermissionRequest, WorktreeCreate, and one side-effect event (SessionStart).
- Existing scope-lock tests continue to pass without modification (PreToolUse rendering is unchanged from the outside).

title: Empirical-Bayes learned prior is computed but dropped (never reaches the projection)
description:
cch.forecast/window-priors merges learned-prior (which returns {:mu :sigma}) onto the window-config baseline (which uses {:prior-mu :prior-sigma}), but compute-window-stats and build-current-window destructure :prior-mu/:prior-sigma — so the learned prior's :mu/:sigma are silently dropped and every projection anchors on the hardcoded baseline. The empirical-Bayes machinery (weighted-prior-params, historical-finals-sql, learned-prior) is effectively dead code; a test even pins the drop as intended.

Fix: in window-priors, when learned-prior returns >=2-window params, remap :mu/:sigma -> :prior-mu/:prior-sigma so the learned values actually override the baseline. THEN extend learning to the 5h window (currently 7d-only): generalize weighted-prior-params to divide final_pct by the window's hours (168 for 7d, 5 for 5h), make historical-finals-sql/learned-prior window-key aware, and pass 5h historical-finals into window-info. Context: 242 completed 5h + 19 completed 7d windows are available on the collector. Verify projections don't regress against known windows before/after.

Note: baseline constants were data-grounded (5h 3.75/1.3, 7d 0.42/0.13) as the cold-start fallback in the same change that filed this; this issue makes the priors ADAPT over time rather than stay static.
close_reason: Lever A: window-priors now applies the empirical-Bayes learned prior (per agent, per window) as :prior-mu/:prior-sigma, replacing the old (merge base learned) that dropped it under :mu/:sigma. Extended learning to the 5h window (window-json-key/window-hours maps; historical-finals-sql, historical-final-pcts, learned-prior all window-key aware). window-config demoted to cold-start seed (used only until ≥2 completed windows exist). projections.clj fallback defaults aligned to 0.42/0.13. Verified live: 7d μ=0.413, 5h μ=3.97 computed from real completed windows.

title: beads git hooks can't export memory-inclusive jsonl → jsonl-only sync not portable
description: Define a JSONL-first Beads synchronization workflow that is safe across multiple repositories and concurrent agents, with explicit export, import, and conflict behavior.
design:
WORKAROUND (deployed): append the jsonl-only logic to the git-TRACKED .beads/hooks/ shims, placed AFTER the beads-managed BEGIN/END block so (a) it ships via git and is portable, (b) it has the final say on issues.jsonl, and (c) it survives 'bd hooks install' (which only rewrites between the markers). Set core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks per clone (beads sets this during init). pre-commit runs 'bd export --all' + git add; post-merge/post-checkout run 'bd import' (safe upsert); pre-push left to beads' shim (no-op under dolt.local-only=true).

REAL UPSTREAM FIX (not in this repo): beads should support a memory-inclusive export from its hook path — e.g. an 'export.scope=all' config honored by 'bd hooks run pre-commit', or make the shrink guard memory-aware. Until then the workaround above is the portable mechanism.
notes: Repository names, local database ports, and private coordination details were removed; only the reusable synchronization model remains.
close_reason: Documented and deployed the generic JSONL-first hook workflow; upstream memory-inclusive export remains a separate feature request.

title: bd auto-starts rogue per-project Dolt servers in shared-server mode
description:
In shared-Dolt-server mode (one sql-server, one database per repo, all repos pointing at a fixed port), bd auto-starts a throwaway per-project dolt server on a random port whenever the configured port is momentarily unreachable — most commonly during a shared-server restart. Problems this causes:

1. The rogue server lingers after the command exits, serving stale/empty local data.
2. bd writes a .beads/dolt-server.port file pinning the repo to that random port, which then OVERRIDES metadata.json (the port file is 'primary'), so subsequent commands keep hitting the dead rogue port even after the shared server is back ('database X not found on server at 127.0.0.1:<random>').
3. It masks the real target and produces confusing 'not found' errors.

Mitigation applied during rollout: pin the shared port in every repo (metadata dolt_server_port + .beads/dolt-server.port both set to the shared 3307) and kill stray servers.

Options: (a) a connect-only / no-auto-start config for shared-server setups; (b) never let an auto-start port overwrite an explicitly-pinned port; (c) reap rogue servers on exit; (d) when the configured port is briefly down, retry/backoff instead of spawning a new server.

title: Dolt schema-migration self-block when importing an old-schema beads DB onto a shared server
description:
When an older-schema beads Dolt database is placed under a running dolt sql-server (e.g. migrating a per-project DB into a shared-server data-dir), the first bd command triggers a schema migration that ALTERs tables but leaves the working set dirty because dolt auto-commit is off by default. bd then refuses to proceed ('pending schema migrations alter pre-existing dirty tables: ...; run bd dolt commit'), but 'bd dolt commit' itself cannot open the DB for the same reason — a self-block (upstream gastownhall/beads#4566).

Repro: move a per-project .beads/dolt DB dir into a shared sql-server data-dir, restart the server, run 'bd stats' in the repo.

Workaround used during the shared-server rollout: commit the working set server-side over the MySQL protocol — CALL DOLT_COMMIT('-Am', 'finalize schema migration') on the affected database — after which bd migrates cleanly and all issues are intact.

Options: (a) document in a shared-server migration runbook; (b) ship a helper that performs the server-side commit; (c) push upstream so the migration auto-commits its own working set.
notes: root-cause pass: verifying auto-export reconciliation

title: Three tests fail on macOS: /private path canonicalization + hardcoded Linux home
description: Suite is green on Linux but has 3 failures on macOS, all test-only portability issues (not product bugs): (1) scope_lock_test expects /tmp/scratch.py allowed, but macOS canonicalizes /tmp to /private/tmp so check-scope's canonicalized path differs from the literal expected; (2) server_test git-root-on-disk-finds-nearest-worktree compares a /var/folders temp path against the canonicalized /private/var/folders result; (3) attention_test render-reports-figures hardcodes a Linux home path in its fixture, so the home-abbreviator (which uses host user.home) leaves it un-abbreviated on macOS. The hardcoded home also violates the repo's no-username-paths rule. Fix: canonicalize expected paths in the path tests; derive home from System/getProperty user.home in the attention fixture.

title: cch install/uninstall silently ignore unknown flags (e.g. --help runs a real install)
description: cli.install/run parses flags but only branches on --codex/--agy/--global; any other flag falls through to the :else branch and performs a real mutating install. So 'cch install --help' does not print help — it runs the default Claude install and rewrites settings.local.json. Same for run-uninstall. Fix: recognize --help/-h and print usage; reject unknown flags with an error + non-zero exit instead of silently proceeding. Known flags: --codex, --agy, --global.
acceptance_criteria: cch install --help prints usage and mutates nothing; cch install --bogus errors with exit 2; --codex/--agy/--global still work; same for uninstall; tests cover help + unknown-flag paths.
close_reason: Fixed in b53cc33: --help/-h print usage, unknown flags error with exit 2 before any mutation; cli.install-test added. Full suite green.

title: Server should self-recover from posix_spawn/fork failures after in-place JDK upgrade
description: A long-lived cch server JVM can lose the ability to fork child processes (e.g. git) after the JDK is upgraded in place underneath the running process (Homebrew brew upgrade openjdk, or a package-manager JDK bump on Linux). Symptom: every hook that shells out to git throws 'Cannot run program git: posix_spawn failed, error: 0 (none)', flooding the server log while the JVM stays up serving, so hooks silently fail. Observed on macOS after ~1 month uptime; the same exposure exists on Linux. Confirmed fix: restart the JVM (launchctl kickstart / systemd restart) so it re-binds to the current JDK on disk. Preventive options to evaluate: (1) health check that detects repeated spawn failures and triggers a self-restart or emits a loud alert instead of silently flooding the log; (2) launch the JVM with -Djdk.lang.Process.launchMechanism=FORK as a fallback launch mechanism; (3) a post-JDK-upgrade hook that restarts the service. The launchd/systemd unit was already hardened to capture install-time PATH. Decide which layer(s) to implement.

title: Federate cch event log across machines via central collector on a VPS
description: cch runs on several machines, each with a local SQLite event log at ~/.local/share/cch/events.db. Goal: a unified, queryable view of hook activity across all machines, without breaking the sub-50ms fire-and-forget local write hot path and without the unsafe shared-SQLite-file-over-network approach (network fs locking corrupts SQLite). Design: central-collector on an always-on, publicly reachable VPS. Each node keeps its local SQLite unchanged (hot path preserved); a periodic job ships new append-only rows since a per-node watermark (WHERE id greater than last_shipped) to an ingest endpoint on the VPS. Ingest is single-writer (safe SQLite) and idempotent on (node,id). Schema change: add a node column to events and context_snapshots so rows are attributable; keep local AUTOINCREMENT id since (node,id) is globally unique. events and context_snapshots are append-only, so aggregation is union-of-appends with no conflict resolution. hook_config is the only table with real updates; handle separately with last-writer-wins on updated_at if shared config is later wanted. Transport can reuse the existing HTTP dispatcher on port 8888 (nodes POST row batches). Multi-master tech (cr-sqlite, Dolt) is only needed if near-live shared state is later required; not needed for the aggregate-analytics use case.
design: Transport: Tailscale tailnet. Collector binds cch serve to its tailnet interface (--host <tailnet-ip>), so /ingest is reachable only by tailnet devices over WireGuard — no public exposure, traffic already encrypted. App-level bearer token optional (enforced iff configured) as defense-in-depth. Schema: events + context_snapshots get node TEXT (origin machine, defaults to hostname, stamped at write) and origin_id INTEGER (source row id, set only on ingested rows); UNIQUE(node, origin_id) gives idempotent INSERT OR IGNORE while local rows keep autoincrement id (origin_id NULL, NULLs distinct in SQLite unique index). Watermark per table in local federation_offsets table. Shipper: background loop reads WHERE id>watermark, POSTs batches to collector-url, advances watermark. All deployment specifics (collector-url, token, node override) in ~/.config/cch/config.yaml federation: section — nothing private in the repo.
close_reason: Federation mechanism delivered in b307ec0: node/origin_id schema + migrations, cch.federation (identity/config/idempotent ingest/watermark), cch.federation.ship (daemon shipper via http-kit), POST /ingest (collector-only + optional bearer token), lifecycle wiring, node queryable via query-events. Config is opt-in in ~/.config/cch/config.yaml, nothing private in repo. 8 new tests + live smoke test (401/200/idempotent) all green; full suite 304/0. Dashboard node-column surfacing split to a follow-up.

title: Coalesce duplicate AGY status-line snapshots
description: AGY invokes its status-line command roughly every 300ms while working, producing long runs of identical quota/context payloads and unnecessary context_snapshots rows. Add bounded server-side coalescing for agent=agy that records material quota changes immediately while retaining a periodic heartbeat for unchanged payloads.
design: Coalesce at the server ingestion boundary so the behavior is independent of shell timing and protects the database even if multiple AGY processes invoke the adapter. Use an in-memory per-session state with atomic updates, a 30-second heartbeat, and a signature containing canonical rate_limits plus relevant context counters. Bound stale state to prevent unbounded session growth.
acceptance_criteria: Identical AGY quota/context payloads within the debounce window create one row; material quota changes are captured immediately; unchanged payloads are accepted with HTTP 204 and captured again after the heartbeat interval; other agents are unaffected; concurrency behavior is deterministic; tests pass; deployed service is verified against repeated live-style payloads.
notes: Observed live AGY bursts at ~300ms with identical quota/context payloads. Implemented atomic per-session server coalescing: first payload, quota changes, transition into idle, and 30-second heartbeats are stored; intervening emissions return 204 with X-CCH-Captured:false. State expires after 24h and is bounded to 256 sessions. Tests: 291 tests / 750 assertions pass in bounded groups; changed-file lint clean. Live verification: five identical posts returned true,false,false,false,false and produced exactly one row; smoke row removed. Runtime deployed and systemd service restarted.
close_reason: AGY snapshots are coalesced with immediate quota/idle captures and a 30-second heartbeat; tests and live deployment verified.

title: Add AGY quota capture to usage dashboard
description: AGY (Antigravity CLI) exposes Claude-like lifecycle hooks, but quota data arrives through its statusLine JSON payload. Add a durable AGY status-line adapter that posts snapshots to CCH with X-CCH-Agent: agy, normalize AGY quota buckets into the existing canonical rate_limits shape, expose AGY as a source on /usage, and provide an install path that replaces the currently missing temporary statusline command without blocking AGY when CCH is unavailable.
design: Use AGY's documented statusLine feed for quota capture rather than scraping the interactive /usage panel. Convert remaining_fraction to used_percentage and reset_time to resets_at. Keep lifecycle hook adapter work in the parent issue; this child is the quota/usage slice.
acceptance_criteria: Official AGY hook and quota interfaces are documented; AGY status-line payloads are normalized to canonical rate-limit snapshots; /usage accepts and renders agent=agy; installation configures a durable command and preserves useful status rendering; unit/integration tests pass; live local capture is verified when an AGY status payload is emitted.
notes: Research: official AGY docs confirm lifecycle command hooks in workspace .agents/hooks.json or global ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json, with PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PreInvocation/PostInvocation/Stop and camelCase JSON payloads. Quota is separately exposed by the documented ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json statusLine feed as model/bucket entries containing remaining_fraction, reset_time, and reset_in_seconds. Implemented quota slice via durable non-blocking status-line adapter, weekly-to-seven_day normalization, /usage AGY tab, idempotent install/restore, tests, live deployment, and end-to-end smoke verification (6.22% normalized; page 18ms). Lifecycle hook routing remains in parent zby.
close_reason: AGY status-line quota capture, normalization, usage tab, install/restore flow, tests, live deployment, and smoke verification completed.

title: Optimize exact counts for filtered events views
description: After fixing unfiltered /events, profiling still shows high-volume exact filter aggregates are slower: hook=event-log about 2.8s, since about 0.84s, and cwd-prefix about 1.6s on the 1.07M-row database. decision-counts and cwd-scoped recent-sessions can scan large index/table ranges. Choose query hints, targeted covering indexes, caching, or summary data without materially increasing hook-write latency.

The current window build repeatedly JSON-extracts rate-limit fields and runs multiple windowed scans over payload. Evaluate denormalized rate-limit columns/indexes or a consolidated query while preserving forecast results.

title: 5h projection chart renders flat despite non-zero projected delta
description:
On /usage?window=5h the projection line appears flat even though /forecast returns a non-trivial delta:

  five_hour: current_pct=31, projected_pct=54.1, band={lo:53, hi:55}, local_rate_phr=-3.0

A 31→54 slope over the remaining ~2h should be visibly slanted. Hypotheses to investigate:

1. **Chart scaling.** y-axis caps at 125 (cch.usage/y-max). A 23-pt rise on that scale across the small horizontal span of "now → resets-at" may look near-flat. Compare to the 7d chart where 7 days of horizontal span amplifies the slope.

2. **last-pct vs projection-anchor mismatch.** chart-svg's `line-for` uses `last-pct` as the now-side anchor:
     `(line-for proj-pct) → [[proj-x0 (sy last-pct)] [proj-x1 (sy proj-pct)]]`
   If `last-pct` in the bundle differs from `current_pct` shown in the tile, the line could start from a different y than the user expects.

3. **Negative local_rate_phr** suggests a recent 5h reset. The build-current-window logic shifts resets-at forward when the stored one has passed, but `last-pct` (= `:pct (last in-window)`) may still hold the pre-reset value of ~90% if the post-reset sample hasn't been written yet. Anchor at 90 with projection at 54 would render as a flat line (or descending) rather than the user-expected slope from current=31.

4. **Burn-rate display** shows -3.0%/h — actionable noise. After a reset, a brief period of "negative burn rate" is meaningless and probably should be suppressed (clamp at 0 for display, or show "—" when the window contains a reset).

## Acceptance

- Reproduce locally: GET /forecast and /usage?window=5h, compare current_pct, last_pct (from build-current-window), and what the chart actually draws.
- Either fix the underlying anchor mismatch, or document why current_pct ≠ last-pct is intentional.
- Bonus: clip negative burn-rate display to 0 / "—" so post-reset spikes don't surface as misleading numbers.

## Context

Discovered while smoke-testing claude-code-hooks-429 (per-agent /usage tab). 7d projection looks normal (94→98, +4 over 4d = clearly slanted). Issue is specific to the 5h window's display.
close_reason: Root cause: build-current-window (the /usage chart path) called proj/rate-bayes-projection without passing window-specific priors via window-info. rate-bayes-projection's hardcoded defaults are tuned for 7d (μ=0.55 %/hr, σ=0.045), so for 5h the prior overwhelmed observation and the projected_pct stuck near last_pct. compute-window-stats (the /forecast statusline path) was passing priors correctly. Fix: extracted window-priors helper from compute-window-stats, called from both. Live verification: 5h projection line now slopes 34.8px (was 3px). /usage and /forecast now produce matching projections by construction.

title: Investigate Codex trusted_hash scheme; write hashes from cch install
description:
Codex gates every hook handler behind a 'trusted_hash' field on HookHandlerConfig (binary string analysis confirms; --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust skips the check). When cch install --codex writes a hook, we have two paths:

A. Reproduce Codex's hashing scheme and write trusted_hash directly. User sees no trust prompt on first run.

B. Skip the hash; user gets a one-time trust prompt from Codex itself. Simpler, but worse UX, and breaks non-interactive setups.

## Investigation steps

1. Find an existing trusted hook in someone's config (or trust a dummy hook via Codex once) and inspect the resulting trusted_hash format. Look at HookStateToml — likely stored in ~/.codex/ somewhere separate from config.toml.
2. Determine what's hashed: handler command? plus matcher? plus event name? plus scope? Probably a stable canonical serialization.
3. Determine the hash algorithm (sha256 likely).
4. If reproducible, implement the hasher in src/cch/agents/codex.clj.
5. If too fragile (e.g. depends on internal Codex versioning), fall back to path B with a clear message.

## Acceptance

- cch install --codex completes such that next 'codex exec' runs the hook without prompting OR
- cch install --codex prints a clear one-liner the user can copy/paste to trust the hook.

## Notes

- Worst case is that the hash includes a Codex-internal version string and we can't reproduce it. Then path B is the answer.
- We can also document --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust as an escape hatch for CI, but should not require it for normal use.
notes:
## CORRECTED conclusion (2026-05-27, second pass)

Earlier 'codex exec doesn't fire hooks' was wrong. The actual gate is the TOFU trust prompt.

**Working sequence:**
1. cch install --codex writes the hook block to ~/.codex/config.toml
2. User runs codex TUI once; codex prompts for trust on the new hooks
3. User approves → trust state persists somewhere (likely ~/.codex/hooks_state.toml per HookStateToml struct)
4. ALL subsequent codex invocations (exec, TUI, etc.) fire the trusted hooks

End-to-end confirmed: codex exec with a shell-tool prompt → 9 events landed in cch DB with agent='codex' (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit ×2, PreToolUse Bash ×3, PostToolUse Bash ×2, Stop). Codex even surfaces the hook in its own stdout as 'hook: Stop / hook: Stop Completed'.

**The --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust mystery:**

Per discovery.rs the flag should let any enabled hook fire regardless of trust_status. Empirically it printed the warning banner but hooks did not fire. Possible explanations:
- Flag only applies to layers that have some entry in the state BTreeMap; untrusted hooks may be skipped earlier in the discovery flow
- Some other gate we haven't identified
- Worth filing upstream if it bothers users

For cch install --codex, we should document: 'first codex run will prompt to approve the hooks; approve to enable cch integration.'

## What this means for downstream issues

- claude-code-hooks-429 (per-agent usage tile) can now be developed against REAL codex event streams, not just synthetic
- All multi-CLI plumbing is verified working
close_reason: Schema captured, install path correct, end-to-end verified post-TOFU. --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust empirically didn't help (warning printed but hooks still skipped) but the trust-via-TUI path works fine. Hash reproduction not needed for v1 — user approves once via codex's own prompt.

title: TOML reader/writer for Codex ~/.codex/config.toml with cch tagging
description:
Codex config is TOML, not JSON. Need a sibling to src/cch/settings.clj that:

- Reads ~/.codex/config.toml preserving comments and key order where possible.
- Writes hook entries under `[[hooks.<EventName>]]` arrays with `[[hooks.<EventName>.hooks]]` inside (see schema below).
- Tags cch-managed entries with a `# cch:name` marker line so cch uninstall can find and remove them without disturbing user-written hooks.
- Atomic writes (tmp file + rename) like the JSON path.

## Schema (confirmed from openai/codex source, see 14s notes)

```toml
[[hooks.PreToolUse]]
matcher = ".*"
[[hooks.PreToolUse.hooks]]
type = "command"
command = "curl -s -X POST localhost:8888/<name>"
# optional: timeout, async, statusMessage, commandWindows

[hooks.state."<key>"]
enabled = true
trusted_hash = "<sha-of-NormalizedHookIdentity>"
```

Events: PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop.

## Library choice

- clj-toml or org.tomlj/tomlj — pick whichever preserves comments best. Round-tripping with comments preserved is important since users edit config.toml by hand.

## Acceptance

- cch install --codex doubled-token writes a hook block, leaves rest of config.toml byte-identical except for the inserted section.
- cch uninstall removes only cch-tagged entries.
- Test fixtures cover: empty config, config with existing user hooks, config with prior cch entries.
close_reason: src/cli/codex_settings.clj + tests landed. Sentinel-block approach: '# cch:begin <name>' .. '# cch:end <name>' wraps each cch-managed hook so install/uninstall is pure text splice. Acceptance: install-hook!/remove-hook!/remove-all-cch! exposed; 11 tests covering empty/with-user-content/idempotent-reinstall/coexisting-blocks/preserves-non-cch-user-hooks. Install command wiring belongs to cdt.

title: Agent adapter layer: src/cch/agents/{claude_code,codex,gemini}.clj
description:
Introduce a thin per-agent adapter namespace that handles the two things that differ across CLIs: config-file shape and event-name aliasing.

## Per-adapter responsibilities

1. **Settings file**: read/write the agent's config (settings.json for Claude/Gemini, config.toml for Codex). Atomic writes + cch tagging like today's src/cch/settings.clj.
2. **Payload normalize**: agent payload (already mostly identical) -> common map with canonical event names. Gemini's BeforeTool/AfterTool -> PreToolUse/PostToolUse; Codex's SessionStart variants -> {:event :session-start :source :startup|:resume|:clear|:compact}.
3. **Install/uninstall**: writes the hook entry. For Claude this stays HTTP-type; for Codex/Gemini, points at the shim binary with the right env vars.

## Common map shape (tentative)

```clojure
{:agent           :claude-code | :codex | :gemini
 :event           :pre-tool-use | :post-tool-use | :session-start | ...
 :session-id      string
 :transcript-path string
 :cwd             string
 :tool-name       string  ; for tool events
 :tool-input      map
 :raw             original-payload-map}  ; for adapter-specific access
```

## Dispatcher changes

- HTTP server routes on event name only; the X-CCH-Agent header selects the adapter for normalization on the way in.
- defhook check fns receive the common map and remain agent-agnostic.

## Acceptance

- Existing Claude Code hooks pass tests unchanged after migrating through the adapter.
- One worked example each for Codex + Gemini (e.g. the doubled-token detector firing on all three).
notes:
## Status (2026-05-27)

Codex slice landed in commit 3a39022:
- src/cch/agents/codex.clj writes a single sentinel block of curl entries to ~/.codex/config.toml
- cch install --codex / cch uninstall --codex wired in

- 8 unit tests passing

Remaining work split to claude-code-hooks-zby:

title: Build cch-hook-shim: tiny binary that POSTs stdin JSON to localhost:8888
description:
Codex and Gemini hook configs only support 'command' handler type — no native HTTP. To run their hooks inside the long-running cch server (preserving the <50ms budget), we need a small shim binary the config can point at.

## Behavior

- Read JSON payload from stdin.
- Read CCH_EVENT env var (or argv[1]) for the event name, e.g. PreToolUse.
- Read CCH_AGENT env var (or argv[2]) for the source agent: claude-code | codex | gemini.
- POST to http://localhost:8888/<event> with the JSON body + a header like X-CCH-Agent.
- Forward server's HTTP status to exit code: 200 -> 0, 422 (deny) -> 2, etc.
- Forward response body to stdout (so the agent CLI parses it as the hook result).
- Forward any server-supplied stderr lines back through stderr.
- On connection failure: exit 0 with empty stdout (fail open — never block the agent because cch is down).

## Acceptance

- Single static binary, no runtime deps. Go (~3 MB) or Rust preferred.
- Cold-start latency under 30ms on typical hardware.
- Works as the 'command' field value in Codex config.toml and Gemini settings.json.
- Tested against the existing cch dispatcher end-to-end.
notes:
RESOLVED: no shim binary needed. The shim is one curl invocation.

## Benchmark (cch on localhost:8888, hyperfine 30 runs each)

| approach              | total       | server | shim overhead |
|-----------------------|-------------|--------|---------------|
| curl                  | 9.6 ms      | 2.8 ms | ~7 ms         |
| ncat + bash + awk     | 22.2 ms     | 2.8 ms | ~19 ms        |
| (Claude in-proc HTTP) | ~0 (no spawn)| -      | 0             |

curl wins: single binary, ubiquitous, native HTTP, fail-open friendly.

## Recommended hook config value

For Codex (config.toml) and Gemini/agy (settings.json) install paths:

  command = \"curl -sS --max-time 1 --data-binary @- http://localhost:8888/dispatch/<EventName>\"

- -sS = quiet but show errors on stderr
- --max-time 1 = never block the agent more than 1 s if cch is wedged
- --data-binary @- = stream stdin payload through unchanged
- exits 0 on 2xx (continue); response body forwarded to stdout where
  Codex/Gemini parse it for {decision: deny, reason: ...}

For fail-open on cch-down, append: ' 2>/dev/null || true'

## Implications

- No custom shim binary to build, sign, or distribute.
- No UDS listener changes to the cch server.
- The original socat/nc fallback plumbing in this issue's earlier
  design is now moot — curl is the universal default.
- cdt (adapter layer) no longer depends on bp0 in any meaningful way;
  install just writes the curl one-liner.
close_reason: Spike proved curl is sufficient (9.6 ms); no shim binary needed.

title: Multi-CLI support: extend cch beyond Claude Code (Codex, Gemini)
description:
## Goal

Broaden cch so the same hook check functions, dispatcher, event log, and usage estimator serve multiple agentic CLIs — starting with OpenAI Codex and Google Gemini, in addition to Claude Code. Keep the repo name and 'cch' package name for now; rename only if/when the multi-agent abstraction lands cleanly.

## Why this is feasible

All three CLIs converged on essentially the same hook contract:

| Field | Claude Code | Codex | Gemini |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event names | PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, SubagentStop, PreCompact, UserPromptSubmit, Notification, Stop | PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionStart (startup/resume/clear/compact), SubagentStart, SubagentStop | BeforeTool, AfterTool, SessionStart, etc. (Gemini ships 'gemini hooks migrate --from-claude') |
| Payload | JSON on stdin: session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name, tool_input, ... | JSON on stdin: same field names | JSON on stdin: same field names + timestamp |
| Decision | exit 2 + stderr OR stdout JSON {decision} | same | same (decision: allow/deny, reason) |
| Config | settings.json (JSON) | config.toml (TOML) | settings.json (JSON) |
| Handler types | command, http (Claude-only) | command, agent, prompt | command only |

So a single defhook check fn — receiving a normalized payload map — can serve all three. Diverging surfaces:

1. Config format: TOML for Codex vs JSON for Claude/Gemini.
2. Transport: Claude has native HTTP handler type; Codex and Gemini are command-only. A thin shim binary (POST stdin to localhost:8888) fills the gap with one extra process spawn (~5-30ms with a compiled shim).
3. Codex 'trusted_hash' trust gate: TOFU hash of each handler config entry; cch install needs to either prompt the user to trust on first invocation or reproduce Codex's hashing scheme and write the hash directly.
4. Event name aliasing: Gemini uses BeforeTool/AfterTool; adapter normalizes to PreToolUse/PostToolUse internally.

## Payoff

- One usage-estimation pipeline across all CLIs the user runs, fed by a shared SQLite events table with an :agent discriminator column.
- One implementation of the doubled-token detector, the project-scope check, etc. — wins on every CLI for free.
- Per-agent breakdowns of usage / hook activity fall out of the same projection.

## Out of scope (for this epic)

- Repo/package rename — defer until the abstraction proves out.
- Anthropic-specific Notification event semantics (no Codex/Gemini equivalent).
- Anthropic 'Antigravity' CLI (successor to gemini) — file separately if/when it ships.

## Child issues to follow

- shim binary for HTTP-less CLIs
- src/cch/agents/ adapter layer (claude-code, codex, gemini)
- TOML reader/writer for Codex config
- payload normalizer + :agent discriminator on events table
- cch install --codex / --gemini
- Codex trusted_hash investigation + writer (or trust-prompt UX)
- port doubled-token + scope checks to common payload shape
- update usage estimator to group-by :agent
notes: Phase 1 work landed: usage page 5h/7d toggle is now a child issue. Multi-CLI default selection (5h for codex, 7d for claude) waits on 9a2 (:agent column).

title: feat: script-judge agent hook for LLM-assisted command safety
description:
Add a script-judge hook that uses Haiku/Sonnet to reason about whether a script execution command (uv run python foo.py, python script.py, node script.js) is safe to auto-allow, replacing blanket allow/deny with per-script judgment.

## Motivation

Blanket-denying 'uv run' blocks legitimate non-destructive scripts and requires constant human approval. Blanket-allowing it grants general machine control. An LLM can read the actual script and reason about safety in ~1-2s — fast enough for a permission check, cheap enough to run on Haiku.

## Design

Two-stage pipeline:

  command-guard (:code hook, <1ms)
    known-dangerous pattern → :deny immediately (no LLM)
    matches judgment-tier pattern → pass through (no decision)

  script-judge (:agent hook, Haiku)
    extracts script path from command string
    reads script contents via Read tool
    reasons about: file writes, subprocess spawning, external network calls
    returns :allow (silent, unattended) / :ask / :deny with reason

## Judgment criteria

Non-destructive signals (allow): pure data transforms, reading files, stdout output, localhost network, read-only DB queries

Destructive signals (ask/deny):
  - open(..., 'w'/'a'), shutil.rmtree, os.remove → file writes
  - subprocess, os.system, os.popen, shlex → spawns subprocesses
  - requests/httpx/urllib to external hosts → external network
  - sys.argv manipulation, argparse with write-path args → indirect writes

## Registry wiring

- script-judge registered as :agent type with :agent-model haiku and :agent-prompt-template
- Matcher pattern: 'uv run python|python\s+\S+\.py|node\s+\S+\.js' (tunable per-repo via .cch-config.yaml)
- command-guard matcher unchanged — it only hard-denies, never escalates
- script-judge fires independently on the same PreToolUse event

## Fallbacks

- Script path not found or unreadable → :ask (fail cautious)
- Agent call exceeds timeout → :ask
- Script is a compiled binary / not Python/JS → :ask

## Broader context

This is the first step toward a CCH-native 'auto mode' — unattended operation where dangerous things are hard-denied by code hooks and ambiguous things are judged by a fast LLM, leaving only genuinely novel situations for human review. Blanket permission configs (like Claude Code built-in auto mode) are the alternative but sacrifice the safety floor that CCH provides.
design: Separate hook from command-guard (stays pure/fast). Agent hook reads script before deciding. Haiku preferred for cost/speed; Sonnet as fallback for complex scripts. Decision cached per script+content-hash within session to avoid re-judging the same file. Per-repo extra-patterns in .cch-config.yaml can extend or restrict the judgment-tier matcher.

title: Diagnose sparse context_snapshots writes during active sessions
description:
During a 7+ hour workday Apr 24 with 4-6 concurrent Claude Code sessions, only ~22 rows landed in context_snapshots — far fewer than expected from observed statusLine refresh cadence (visible changes every few minutes per session).

The EWMA pace number (read from these snapshots) appeared unresponsive yesterday and then jumped 83→107% overnight, which is consistent with a long gap (last sample 17:46 PDT, next 14:23 PDT next day) where dt ≫ tau, so the EWMA effectively snaps to whatever rate the lone new sample implies.

Server is fine: cch dev server (port 8888) was up the whole time, /ewma and POST /context-snapshot both work, snapshot row IDs are sequential (no writer-queue drops). So the loss is either upstream of the server or in a path we haven't instrumented.
design:
Hypothesis A (statusLine doesn't fire as often as we think) is contradicted by user observation of frequent statusline updates across multiple sessions. Hypothesis B (POST is failing silently) is plausible but the original 'curl & gets killed' theory was unsupported — bash doesn't SIGHUP background jobs in non-interactive shells and Claude Code reading EOF doesn't kill the process group.

Decision: instrument first, theorize later. Added two log lines to ~/.claude/statusline-command.sh — one before the curl (invocation), one after (curl exit code + HTTP status), both to ~/.cch-statusline.log.
notes:
Diagnostic queries after a day of use:

  wc -l ~/.cch-statusline.log
  grep -c '^[0-9.]* invoke' ~/.cch-statusline.log   # script fires
  grep -c 'http=204' ~/.cch-statusline.log          # successful POSTs
  sqlite3 ~/.local/share/cch/events.db \
    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM context_snapshots WHERE timestamp > datetime('now','-1 day');"

Outcomes:
- invoke ≈ snapshots ≈ http=204 → statusLine genuinely fires less often than perceived. Settles the question.
- invoke ≫ http=204 → curl is failing or being interrupted. rc and missing-result lines pinpoint how.
- invoke ≈ http=204 ≫ snapshots → server accepting but losing on writer-queue side. Investigate bb writer.

Side finding (separate from this bug): used_pct column is NULL on every real snapshot but populated on test/probe rows. Real Claude Code payload's .context_window.used_percentage is absent or null at write time. Doesn't affect EWMA (reads JSON blob). Worth a separate issue if it matters.

title: dashboard: live event stream via Datastar + SSE (and drop Apply button)
description:
# Live event dashboard via Datastar + SSE

## Context

Dashboard currently requires manual refresh (Cmd+R) to see new events. For an observability tool with multiple concurrent Claude Code sessions firing hooks, that feels wrong — you expect the pane to update. User already uses Datastar in other projects; the pattern is a natural fit here (one-way push, fragment-merge semantics preserve open details/scroll state).

Also dropping the Apply button: once selects auto-submit on change, the explicit Apply becomes dead weight.

## Scope

### Server

1. Event broadcast in `src/cch/log.clj` or a new `src/cch/events.clj` — an atom of open SSE client channels. New fn `broadcast!` writes to every registered channel, cleaning up closed ones.

2. `wrap-logging` middleware in `src/cch/middleware.clj` — after calling `log-event!`, also render the event-card hiccup and call `broadcast!` with the HTML fragment. Non-blocking; broadcast failures dont bubble up.

3. New route `GET /events/stream` in `src/cch/server.clj` — uses httpkits `http/as-channel` to keep the connection open, subscribes to broadcast, emits `datastar-merge-fragments` SSE frames as events arrive. Sets `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, disables buffering.

4. SSE frame helpers — hand-rolled, ~15 LOC. Datastars protocol is `event: datastar-merge-fragments\ndata: selector .event-list\ndata: mergeMode prepend\ndata: fragments <article...>\n\n`. Lift the exact constants from starfederation/datastar Clojure SDK, do not add the dep.

### Client

5. Dashboard head adds `<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/starfederation/datastar@main/bundles/datastar.js"></script>` (or pinned version equivalent).

6. `.event-list` gets `data-on-load="@get(/events/stream)"` so the SSE connection opens on page load.

7. Filter selects get `onchange="this.form.submit()"` so choosing a filter reloads the page immediately. The Apply button is removed. Text/number inputs (Since, Limit) either keep a submit trigger or go through Datastar `data-on-input__debounce.500ms` — decide when implementing.

### Filter-awareness

v1: broadcast is global — every connected client gets every event. If the user has a filter active, the stream still prepends rows that do not match (they show until next page reload). Accept this limitation for v1. Follow-up would be per-client filtered streams keyed on query params.

## Non-goals

- No polling fallback
- No filter-aware streams (v1 broadcasts everything)
- No matrix page real-time (config rarely changes; manual toggles fine)
- No WebSocket upgrade path (SSE is sufficient for one-way push)

## Files

- `src/cch/server.clj` — new `/events/stream` route, Datastar script tag, attribute additions
- `src/cch/middleware.clj` — publish to broadcast after `log-event!`
- New: `src/cch/events.clj` or similar — broadcast atom + `subscribe!` / `broadcast!` helpers + SSE frame writer
- `test/cch/server_test.clj` — smoke test that `/events/stream` returns text/event-stream and the connection stays open briefly

## Acceptance

- Load /, keep it open, run `curl -XPOST http://127.0.0.1:8888/dispatch/PreToolUse -d {...}`
- Within 1 second, the new event appears at the top of the list without a page reload
- Existing open `<details>` stay open; scroll position stays put
- Filter selects auto-submit on change; Apply button is gone
- 127+ tests pass with the stream smoke test added

## Notes

Hand-roll SSE frames instead of pulling the Datastar Clojure SDK — its ~100 LOC of thin string-formatting; copying the constants is cleaner for a bb project.
close_reason: Shipped. Datastar + SSE live stream; cch.events pub/sub; wrap-logging publishes to subscribers; GET /events/stream keeps the connection open and emits datastar-patch-elements frames with .event-list prepend; Datastar CDN pin v1.0.0-RC.8 (current). Also dropped the Apply button — selects auto-submit on change via native onchange. Enriched event cards with repo · branch (origin-URL derived, 30s TTL cache), swapped out noisy trailing columns for one context cell. Added emerald fishing-hook favicon + nav glyph. Dual-stack :: bind so localhost just works. 11× page-load perf win via SQL aggregation (distinct-cwds, recent-sessions) and indexes.

title: shift cch to server-owned routing + DB config + optional repo-YAML override
description:
# Shift to server-owned routing and config store

## Current model (as of 2026-04-13)

Each hook is installed individually per repo via `cch install <hook>`, which writes per-hook entries into `settings.json` (global or project-level). `cli/registry.clj` is the install-time source of truth; `.cch-config.yaml` files per repo hold hook-specific options. Adding/removing/reconfiguring hooks means editing settings.json and re-installing.

## Proposed model

Invert who owns the routing table. `settings.json` becomes a small stable set of universal entries — one per Claude Code event — all pointing at the `cch serve` HTTP dispatcher. The server then consults its own config to decide which hooks actually run for a given (event, tool, cwd, payload).

## Why

- Web UI becomes trivial: CRUD a DB table, no cross-repo settings.json mutation, no file scanning.
- Adding a hook = add to `registry.clj` + enable in config; no per-repo re-install.
- Disabling a hook is instant; no settings.json churn.
- Matches how `event-log` already works (universal registration by design).
- Aligns with the direction set by commit cd318b9 (HTTP dispatcher + dashboard).

## Config store

SQLite, not YAML. Use the existing `events.db` with a new table roughly:

```sql
CREATE TABLE hook_config (
  hook_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  scope     TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'global' | 'repo:/abs/path'
  enabled   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  options   TEXT,            -- JSON blob of hook-specific settings
  updated_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (hook_name, scope)
);
```

Transactional, queryable, no parse on every dispatch. UI edits the table directly.

## Repo-YAML as authoritative override

`.cch-config.yaml` stays supported but **as a mode switch, not a merge layer**.

Precedence at dispatch time:
1. Repo `.cch-config.yaml` (if present at the repo root) — authoritative for that repo, DB per-repo rows ignored
2. DB per-repo config (UI-edited) — for repos without YAML
3. DB global config — defaults across all repos
4. Hardcoded defaults — baseline

Rationale: a committed YAML is a team agreement; silently merging DB rows on top would make the file stop being trustworthy. UI shows a read-only 'managed by .cch-config.yaml' banner for such repos, with an optional 'import YAML into DB and delete file' migration.

## What `settings.json` looks like after

Something like:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse":       [{"matcher": "*", "hooks": [{"type": "http", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8888/dispatch/PreToolUse"}]}],
    "PostToolUse":      [{"matcher": "*", "hooks": [{"type": "http", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8888/dispatch/PostToolUse"}]}],
    "SessionStart":     [{"hooks": [{"type": "http", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8888/dispatch/SessionStart"}]}]
    // ... one per event type
  }
}
```

Per-tool matchers (`Edit|Write` etc.) move into cch's dispatch logic, keyed on `tool_name` in the payload.

## UI implications

- New page: hook matrix — rows = hooks, columns = scope (global + enabled repos), cells = enabled/disabled toggle and an 'edit options' link.
- Per-hook settings page: form over the `options` JSON blob, schema-driven per hook.
- Status header: 'cch serve running / events logged: N' + 'YAML-managed' badge per repo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `cch install` writes the universal event entries to settings.json (replaces per-hook install).
- [ ] Legacy per-hook `settings.json` entries still work (don't break existing setups). Migration path: `cch migrate-settings` command.
- [ ] `hook_config` table added via schema migration; existing `events.db` picks it up.
- [ ] Dispatch logic consults DB + YAML with the documented precedence.
- [ ] Web UI CRUD for hook_config.
- [ ] Repo YAML detected and honored; UI shows read-only banner for YAML-managed repos.
- [ ] Command-mode transport still works for users who don't want `cch serve` running.
- [ ] `cch serve` down = clear failure mode (Claude Code sees HTTP timeout; document the degradation).

## Non-goals

- No automatic cross-account sync of DB config (local-only).
- No built-in auth on `cch serve`; it remains a localhost-only single-user tool.
- No breaking change to existing hook code — hooks continue to return the same decision maps; only registration and config storage change.

## Decomposition

This is large. Probably breaks into:
1. Schema migration for `hook_config` table + loader
2. Dispatcher: route by event+tool+cwd, consult config
3. Settings.json universal-entry installer (`cch install`)
4. Legacy settings.json migration command
5. Repo-YAML precedence path
6. Web UI: matrix + per-hook form
7. Docs update

File as child issues once we're ready to start.

# Prompt and agent hooks are NATIVE Claude Code types

Clarification after looking up the Claude Code hooks docs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md):

Claude Code supports four hook types in settings.json:

| type | runtime |
|------|---------|
| command | shell subprocess (stdin/stdout JSON) |
| http | POST to URL (what cch serve uses) |
| prompt | Claude Code sends a prompt to a model, parses {decision, reason} from the response |
| agent | Claude Code spawns a subagent with tool access |

**Prompt and agent hooks run inside Claude Code, not inside cch.** They are native settings.json entries; cch never sees them.

## Implication for this issue

The dispatcher model only owns routing for **code hooks** (those registered in cli.registry, running inside cch's process). Prompt and agent hooks are orthogonal — they live as native settings.json entries and Claude Code executes them directly.

This does NOT require changes to phases 1-3:

- Schema (shipped): fine as-is
- Effective-config loader (shipped): fine as-is
- Dispatcher endpoint: only concerns itself with code hooks

This DOES refine phases 4-5:

- **Phase 4 (install-dispatcher):** writes universal per-event HTTP entries for cch. Must leave pre-existing prompt/agent entries in settings.json untouched (cli.settings/add-hook! already scopes its edits to cch-tagged entries, so this works by construction — just needs a test case).
- **Phase 5 (web UI):** UI becomes a unified control plane across all four types, even though the underlying storage differs:

      | Type | Storage | Editor writes to |
      |------|---------|------------------|
      | code (cch-registered) | hook_config table | DB via config-db CRUD |
      | http (external)       | settings.json     | cli.settings/add-hook! :mode :http |
      | prompt                | settings.json     | new :mode :prompt in add-hook! |
      | agent                 | settings.json     | new :mode :agent in add-hook! |

  Users toggle/edit any hook from one page regardless of type.

## Supersedes / relates to

- bq2 ("Support HTTP, prompt, agent handler types") is no longer about *implementing* these types — they're native. bq2 is now about the UI + installer surface for authoring them. Rescope bq2 or close it in favor of a new 'UI for native hook types' issue when we get to phase 5.

## Key prompt-hook fields for settings.json (from docs)

    {
      "type": "prompt",
      "prompt": "Review this Bash command for security risks:\n\n$ARGUMENTS\n\nDoes this command appear safe?",
      "model": "claude-opus-4-1-20250805",    // optional
      "timeout": 30,                             // optional, default 30
      "statusMessage": "Evaluating...",         // optional, spinner text
      "if": "..."                              // optional permission rule
    }

$ARGUMENTS is substituted with the hook input JSON before sending to the model.
